questions.q: What should you determine before opening any import tool?
options: Which browser extension renders CSV files fastest
The object, approximate volume, and source of the data
The org's custom Apex trigger count
Whether Salesforce Classic or Lightning looks better
questions.explain: Planning starts with the object you're loading into, how many records, and where the data comes from — those answers shape every decision after.

questions.q: A team needs to load 500 new Leads from a trade-show spreadsheet. Which tool fits best by default?
options: Data Loader, because every load should use the desktop app
The Data Import Wizard, since it's a simple, smaller job on a supported object
Neither — Leads can only be created one at a time in the UI
The Bulk API command line, since nothing smaller is supported
questions.explain: The Import Wizard is built for exactly this: a guided flow for a supported object, well under its 50,000-record cap.

questions.q: Why check the System Overview page before a large load?
options: It shows which users are currently logged in
It lists every validation rule in the org
It shows data storage and recent API usage, so you can catch a load that won't fit
It is required to unlock the Data Import Wizard
questions.explain: System Overview shows current data storage against the org's limit and API requests used recently — exactly the headroom a large load needs to check first.

questions.q: Which scenario is the strongest sign that Data Loader, not the Import Wizard, is the right tool?
options: Loading 200 Contacts with a handful of standard fields
Loading 2 million records into a custom object with complex field mappings
Loading 50 Leads for a single sales rep
A one-time import of 10 Campaign Members
questions.explain: Data Loader is built for scale, custom objects, and complex mappings — well beyond the Import Wizard's 50,000-record, simpler-mapping design.

questions.q: Why does a planning checklist include a question about duplicates and backups, not just the mechanics of the load?
options: Because Salesforce requires a backup file before any import will run
Because duplicates and unrecoverable bad data are the most common real-world load failures, not tool errors
Because duplicates automatically pause every import job
Because backups are only relevant to Data Loader, never the Import Wizard
questions.explain: Most load problems aren't the tool failing — they're duplicate records piling up or bad data landing with no easy way back, both of which planning catches in advance.
